content: The test image shows a green stem/petiole with dense white cottony mycelium spreading from it — clearly a stem-related disease. Top candidates from stem classes: **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**, **Southern_Blight**, and **Gray_Mold**.

The test image shows:
- A fresh green stem piece placed on brown paper (lab/diagnostic setting)
- Dense, white, cottony/fluffy mycelium spreading from one end of the stem
- No gray-brown coloring (rules out Gray Mold)
- No dark cankers or blackening (rules out Alternaria, Phytophthora)

This white cottony mycelium from a stem is the hallmark of **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** ("white cotton-like mycelium" on infected stems). Southern Blight also has white mycelium, but the reference images showed cankers without the characteristic white cottony mass matching this pattern. The Sclerotinia KB description — "water-soaked areas covered with white cotton-like mycelium" — matches the test image best.
